sanskrit: kṛṣṇāḥ kanakagauryaś ca nāryaḥ śyāmās tathāparāḥ vayorūpavilāsinyo labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: Women dark of hue, and others golden-fair, and yet others of dusky complexion — graced with youth, beauty, and charm — he wins: of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: yas tu saṃvatsaraṃ bhuṅkte navame navame 'hani sadā dvādaśamāsān vai juhvāno jātavedasam
english: But he who, for a full year, eats only on every ninth day, ever for twelve months pouring oblations into Jātavedas, the fire,

sanskrit: aśvamedhasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ puṇḍarīkaprakāśaṃ ca vimānaṃ labhate naraḥ
english: that man gains the fruit of the horse-sacrifice, and obtains a celestial chariot bright as the white lotus.

sanskrit: dīptasūryāgnitejobhir divyamālābhir eva ca nīyate rudrakanyābhiḥ so 'ntarikṣaṃ sanātanam
english: With the splendor of blazing sun and fire, adorned with heavenly garlands, he is borne aloft by the maidens of Rudra to the eternal firmament.

sanskrit: aṣṭādaśasahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ kalpam eva ca koṭīśatasahasraṃ ca teṣu lokeṣu modate
english: For eighteen thousand years, indeed for an entire aeon, and for a hundred thousand crores of years, he rejoices in those worlds.

sanskrit: yas tu saṃvatsaraṃ bhuṅkte daśāhe vai gate gate sadā dvādaśamāsān vai juhvāno jātavedasam
english: But he who, for a full year, eats only when each tenth day has passed, ever for twelve months pouring oblations into Jātavedas, the fire,

sanskrit: brahmakanyāniveśe ca sarvabhūtamanohare aśvamedhasahasrasya phalaṃ prāpnoty anuttamam
english: in the dwelling of the maidens of Brahmā, enchanting to all beings, attains the unsurpassed fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices.

sanskrit: rūpavatyaś ca taṃ kanyā ramayanti sadā naram nīlotpalanibhair varṇai raktotpalanibhais tathā
english: And lovely maidens ever delight that man, some hued like the blue lotus, others like the red lotus.

sanskrit: vimānaṃ maṇḍalāvartam āvartagahanāvṛtam sāgarormipratīkāśaṃ sādhayed yānam uttamam
english: He wins a supreme celestial chariot, circling in spirals, wreathed in deep whorls, resembling the billows of the ocean.

sanskrit: vicitramaṇimālābhir nāditaṃ śaṅkhapuṣkaraiḥ sphāṭikair vajrasāraiś ca stambhaiḥ sukṛtavedikam ārohati mahad yānaṃ haṃsasārasavāhanam
english: Resounding with strings of wondrous gems, with conches and lotuses, with pillars of crystal and adamantine essence, its terraces finely wrought — he mounts that great chariot drawn by swans and cranes.

sanskrit: ekādaśe tu divase yaḥ prāpte prāśate haviḥ sadā dvādaśamāsān vai juhvāno jātavedasam
english: But he who eats his portion only when the eleventh day has come, ever for twelve months pouring oblations into Jātavedas, the fire,

sanskrit: parastriyo nābhilaṣed vācātha manasāpi vā anṛtaṃ ca na bhāṣeta mātāpitroḥ kṛte 'pi vā
english: who covets not another's wife in word or even in thought, and speaks no falsehood, not even for the sake of mother or father,

sanskrit: abhigacchen mahādevaṃ vimānasthaṃ mahābalam svayaṃbhuvaṃ ca paśyeta vimānaṃ samupasthitam
english: he draws near to Mahādeva the mighty, seated upon his celestial chariot, and beholds the Self-Existent One, his own chariot waiting before him.

sanskrit: kumāryaḥ kāñcanābhāsā rūpavatyo nayanti tam rudrāṇāṃ tam adhīvāsaṃ divi divyaṃ manoharam
english: Maidens of golden radiance and lovely form bear him to that enchanting heavenly abode of the Rudras in the sky.

sanskrit: varṣāṇy aparimeyāni yugāntam api cāvaset koṭīśatasahasraṃ ca daśa koṭiśatāni ca
english: For years beyond measure he dwells there, even to the ending of an age — a hundred thousand crores of years, and ten hundred crores besides.

sanskrit: rudraṃ nityaṃ praṇamate devadānavasaṃmatam sa tasmai darśanaṃ prāpto divase divase bhavet
english: Ever he bows to Rudra, honored by gods and dānavas alike, and day after day he is granted the sight of him.

sanskrit: divase dvādaśe yas tu prāpte vai prāśate haviḥ sadā dvādaśamāsān vai sarvamedhaphalaṃ labhet
english: But he who eats his portion when the twelfth day has come, ever for twelve months, gains the fruit of the all-sacrifice.

sanskrit: ādityair dvādaśais tasya vimānaṃ saṃvidhīyate maṇimuktāpravālaiś ca mahārhair upaśobhitam
english: For him a celestial chariot is fashioned by the twelve Ādityas, made splendid with precious gems, pearls, and corals.

sanskrit: haṃsamālāparikṣiptaṃ nāgavīthīsamākulam mayūraiś cakravākaiś ca kūjadbhir upaśobhitam
english: Encircled by rows of swans, thronged along the elephants' avenue, made beautiful with peacocks and ruddy geese that cry aloud,

sanskrit: aṭṭair mahadbhiḥ saṃyuktaṃ brahmaloke pratiṣṭhitam nityam āvasate rājan naranārīsamāvṛtam ṛṣir evaṃ mahābhāgas tv aṅgirāḥ prāha dharmavit
english: furnished with lofty turrets, established in the world of Brahmā — there forever he dwells, O king, surrounded by men and women. Thus did the illustrious sage Aṅgiras, knower of dharma, declare.

sanskrit: trayodaśe tu divase yaḥ prāpte prāśate haviḥ sadā dvādaśa māsān vai devasatraphalaṃ labhet
english: But he who eats his portion when the thirteenth day has come, ever for twelve months, gains the fruit of the gods' sacrificial session.

sanskrit: raktapadmodayaṃ nāma vimānaṃ sādhayen naraḥ jātarūpaprayuktaṃ ca ratnasaṃcayabhūṣitam
english: That man wins a celestial chariot named 'Rising of the Red Lotus,' wrought of gold and adorned with heaped-up jewels,

sanskrit: devakanyābhir ākīrṇaṃ divyābharaṇabhūṣitam puṇyagandhodayaṃ divyaṃ vāyavyair upaśobhitam
english: thronged with celestial maidens decked in heavenly ornaments, breathing forth holy fragrances, divine, made fair by gentle breezes.

sanskrit: tatra śaṅkupatākaṃ ca yugāntaṃ kalpam eva ca ayutāyutaṃ tathā padmaṃ samudraṃ ca tathā vaset
english: There, where banners fly upon their staffs, he dwells until the ending of an age, indeed an aeon, a myriad of myriads, a padma of years, even an ocean of them.

sanskrit: gītagandharvaghoṣaiś ca bherīpaṇavanisvanaiḥ sadā pramuditas tābhir devakanyābhir īḍyate
english: Amid songs and the strains of gandharvas, the sound of kettledrums and tabors, ever rejoicing, he is praised by those celestial maidens.

sanskrit: caturdaśe tu divase yaḥ pūrṇe prāśate haviḥ sadā dvādaśa māsān vai mahāmedhaphalaṃ labhet
english: But he who eats his portion when the fourteenth day is full, ever for twelve months, gains the fruit of the great sacrifice.

sanskrit: anirdeśyavayorūpā devakanyāḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ mṛṣṭataptāṅgadadharā vimānair anuyānti tam
english: Celestial maidens of indescribable youth and beauty, finely adorned, wearing armlets of burnished gold, follow him in their chariots.

sanskrit: kalahaṃsavinirghoṣair nūpurāṇāṃ ca nisvanaiḥ kāñcīnāṃ ca samutkarṣais tatra tatra vibodhyate
english: By the calls of wild geese, the tinkling of anklets, and the swing and chime of girdle-belts, he is roused now here, now there.

sanskrit: devakanyānivāse ca tasmin vasati mānavaḥ jāhnavīvālukākīrṇe pūrṇaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ naraḥ
english: And in that dwelling of the celestial maidens, strewn with the sands of the Jāhnavī, that man abides for a full year of such reckoning.

sanskrit: yas tu pakṣe gate bhuṅkte ekabhaktaṃ jitendriyaḥ sadā dādaśa māsāṃs tu juhvāno jātavedasam rājasūyasahasrasya phalaṃ prāpnoty anuttamam
english: But he who, when a fortnight has passed, takes a single meal, his senses subdued, ever for twelve months pouring oblations into Jātavedas, the fire, attains the unsurpassed fruit of a thousand royal consecrations.

sanskrit: yānam ārohate nityaṃ haṃsabarhiṇasevitam maṇimaṇḍalakaiś citraṃ jātarūpasamāvṛtam
english: He mounts forever a chariot attended by swans and peacocks, dazzling with circlets of gems, sheathed all in gold,

sanskrit: divyābharaṇaśobhābhir varastrībhir alaṃkṛtam ekastambhaṃ caturdvāraṃ saptabhaumaṃ sumaṅgalam vaijayantīsahasraiś ca śobhitaṃ gītanisvanaiḥ
english: graced by lovely women radiant in heavenly ornaments — single-pillared, four-gated, seven-storied, most auspicious, made splendid by a thousand banners and the sound of song.

sanskrit: divyaṃ divyaguṇopetaṃ vimānam adhirohati maṇimuktāpravālaiś ca bhūṣitaṃ vaidyutaprabham vased yugasahasraṃ ca khaḍgakuñjaravāhanaḥ
english: He ascends that celestial chariot endowed with divine qualities, adorned with gems, pearls, and corals, gleaming like lightning, and there he dwells a thousand ages, borne by rhinoceros and elephant.

sanskrit: ṣoḍaśe divase yas tu saṃprāpte prāśate haviḥ sadā dvādaśa māsān vai somayajñaphalaṃ labhet
english: But he who eats his portion when the sixteenth day has come, ever for twelve months, gains the fruit of the Soma sacrifice.

sanskrit: somakanyānivāseṣu so 'dhyāvasati nityadā saumyagandhānuliptaś ca kāmacāragatir bhavet
english: He dwells forever in the abodes of the daughters of Soma, anointed with gentle fragrances, and moves wherever his will may take him.

sanskrit: sudarśanābhir nārībhir madhurābhis tathaiva ca arcyate vai vimānasthaḥ kāmabhogaiś ca sevyate
english: Seated upon his chariot, he is honored by women fair to look upon and sweet of speech, and is waited upon with every delight of desire.

sanskrit: phalaṃ padmaśataprakhyaṃ mahākalpaṃ daśādhikam āvartanāni catvāri sāgare yāty asau naraḥ
english: His fruit, reckoned as a hundred padmas, lasts a great aeon and ten more; four cycles of the ocean's turning does that man endure.

sanskrit: divase saptadaśame yaḥ prāpte prāśate haviḥ sadā dvādaśa māsān vai juhvāno jātavedasam
english: He who eats his portion when the seventeenth day has come, ever for twelve months pouring oblations into Jātavedas, the fire,

sanskrit: sthānaṃ vāruṇam aindraṃ ca raudraṃ caivādhigacchati mārutauśanase caiva brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: attains the realms of Varuṇa, of Indra, and of Rudra, and reaches the worlds of the Maruts and of Uśanas, and the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: tatra daivatakanyābhir āsanenopacaryate bhūr bhuvaṃ cāpi devarṣiṃ viśvarūpam avekṣate
english: There he is attended with a seat of honor by the maidens of the gods, and beholds earth and mid-air and the divine sage of universal form.

sanskrit: tatra devādhidevasya kumāryo ramayanti tam dvātriṃśad rūpadhāriṇyo madhurāḥ samalaṃkṛtāḥ
english: There the maidens of the God of gods delight him — two-and-thirty in number, of varied forms, sweet of voice and finely adorned.

sanskrit: candrādityāv ubhau yāvad gagane carataḥ prabho tāvac caraty asau vīraḥ sudhāmṛtarasāśanaḥ
english: As long as moon and sun, O lord, journey through the sky, so long does that hero roam, feeding on the nectar-sweet draught of immortality.

sanskrit: aṣṭādaśe tu divase prāśnīyād ekabhojanam sadā dvādaśa māsān vai sapta lokān sa paśyati
english: But he who eats a single meal on the eighteenth day, ever for twelve months, beholds the seven worlds.

sanskrit: rathaiḥ sanandighoṣaiś ca pṛṣṭhataḥ so 'nugamyate devakanyādhirūḍhais tu bhrājamānaiḥ svalaṃkṛtaiḥ
english: He is followed from behind by chariots ringing with joyous sound, gleaming and finely decked, bearing the maidens of the gods.

sanskrit: vyāghrasiṃhaprayuktaṃ ca meghasvananināditam vimānam uttamaṃ divyaṃ susukhī hy adhirohati
english: Yoked with tigers and lions, resounding like a thundercloud, that supreme celestial chariot he mounts in perfect ease.

sanskrit: tatra kalpasahasraṃ sa kāntābhiḥ saha modate sudhārasaṃ ca bhuñjīta amṛtopamam uttamam
english: There for a thousand aeons he rejoices in the company of his beloveds, and feeds on the nectar-draught, supreme and like the elixir of immortality.

sanskrit: ekonaviṃśe divase yo bhuṅkte ekabhojanam sadā dvādaśa māsān vai sapta lokān sa paśyati
english: He who takes a single meal on the nineteenth day, ever for twelve months, beholds the seven worlds.

sanskrit: uttamaṃ labhate sthānam apsarogaṇasevitam gandharvair upagītaṃ ca vimānaṃ sūryavarcasam
english: He gains a supreme abode, attended by hosts of apsarases, and a chariot bright as the sun, hymned by the gandharvas.

sanskrit: tatrāmaravarastrībhir modate vigatajvaraḥ divyāmbaradharaḥ śrīmān ayutānāṃ śataṃ samāḥ
english: There, freed from all fever of grief, he rejoices with the fairest women of the immortals, clad in heavenly raiment and full of splendor, for a hundred myriads of years.

sanskrit: pūrṇe 'tha divase viṃśe yo bhuṅkte hy ekabhojanam sadā dvādaśa māsāṃs tu satyavādī dhṛtavrataḥ
english: And he who takes a single meal when the twentieth day is full, ever for twelve months, speaking truth and steadfast in his vow,

sanskrit: amāṃsāśī brahmacārī sarvabhūtahite rataḥ sa lokān vipulān divyān ādityānām upāśnute
english: eating no flesh, observing chastity, devoted to the welfare of all beings, attains the vast and heavenly worlds of the Ādityas.

sanskrit: gandharvair apsarobhiś ca divyamālyānulepanaiḥ vimānaiḥ kāñcanair divyaiḥ pṛṣṭhataś cānugamyate
english: By gandharvas and apsarases, with heavenly garlands and unguents, in celestial chariots of gold, he is followed from behind.

sanskrit: ekaviṃśe tu divase yo bhuṅkte hy ekabhojanam sadā dvādaśa māsān vai juhvāno jātavedasam
english: He who takes a single meal on the twenty-first day, ever for twelve months pouring oblations into Jātavedas, the fire,

sanskrit: lokam auśanasaṃ divyaṃ śakralokaṃ ca gacchati aśvinor marutāṃ caiva sukheṣv abhirataḥ sadā
english: reaches the heavenly world of Uśanas and the world of Śakra, ever delighting in the joys of the Aśvins and the Maruts.

sanskrit: anabhijñaś ca duḥkhānāṃ vimānavaram āsthitaḥ sevyamāno varastrībhiḥ krīḍaty amaravat prabhuḥ
english: A stranger to all sorrows, seated upon his choice chariot, served by lovely women, he sports like a lord among the immortals.

sanskrit: dvāviṃśe divase prāpte yo bhuṅkte hy ekabhojanam sadā dvādaśa māsān vai juhvāno jātavedasam
english: He who takes a single meal when the twenty-second day has come, ever for twelve months pouring oblations into Jātavedas, the fire,

sanskrit: dhṛtimān ahiṃsānirataḥ satyavāg anasūyakaḥ lokān vasūnām āpnoti divākarasamaprabhaḥ
english: steadfast, devoted to non-injury, truthful and free from envy, attains the worlds of the Vasus, radiant as the day-making sun.

sanskrit: kāmacārī sudhāhāro vimānavaram āsthitaḥ ramate devakanyābhir divyābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ
english: Moving where he wills, feeding on nectar, seated upon his choice chariot, he revels with celestial maidens decked in heavenly ornaments.

sanskrit: trayoviṃśe tu divase prāśed yas tv ekabhojanam sadā dvādaśa māsāṃs tu mitāhāro jitendriyaḥ
english: But he who eats a single meal on the twenty-third day, ever for twelve months, moderate in food and master of his senses,

sanskrit: vāyor uśanasaś caiva rudralokaṃ ca gacchati kāmacārī kāmagamaḥ pūjyamāno 'psarogaṇaiḥ
english: reaches the worlds of Vāyu, of Uśanas, and of Rudra — moving where he wills, going as he desires, honored by hosts of apsarases.

sanskrit: anekaguṇaparyantaṃ vimānavaram āsthitaḥ ramate devakanyābhir divyābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ
english: Seated upon his choice chariot, endowed with manifold excellences, he revels with celestial maidens decked in heavenly ornaments.

sanskrit: caturviṃśe tu divase yaḥ prāśed ekabhojanam sadā dvādaśa māsān vai juhvāno jātavedasam
english: He who eats a single meal on the twenty-fourth day, ever for twelve months pouring oblations into Jātavedas, the fire,

sanskrit: ādityānām adhīvāse modamāno vasec ciram divyamālyāmbaradharo divyagandhānulepanaḥ
english: dwells long, rejoicing, in the abode of the Ādityas, wearing heavenly garlands and raiment, anointed with celestial fragrances.

sanskrit: vimāne kāñcane divye haṃsayukte manorame ramate devakanyānāṃ sahasrair ayutais tathā
english: In a golden, heavenly chariot, swan-yoked and lovely, he revels with thousands and myriads of celestial maidens.

sanskrit: pañcaviṃśe tu divase yaḥ prāśed ekabhojanam sadā dvādaśa māsāṃs tu puṣkalaṃ yānam āruhet
english: But he who eats a single meal on the twenty-fifth day, ever for twelve months, ascends an ample chariot.

sanskrit: siṃhavyāghraprayuktaiś ca meghasvananināditaiḥ rathaiḥ sanandighoṣaiś ca pṛṣṭhataḥ so 'nugamyate
english: By chariots yoked with lions and tigers, resounding like thunderclouds and ringing with joyous sound, he is followed from behind.

sanskrit: devakanyāsamārūḍhai rājatair vimalaiḥ śubhaiḥ vimānam uttamaṃ divyam āsthāya sumanoharam
english: Mounting a supreme, heavenly, most enchanting chariot, escorted by spotless, shining silver ones bearing the maidens of the gods,

sanskrit: tatra kalpasahasraṃ vai vasate strīśatāvṛte sudhārasaṃ copajīvann amṛtopamam uttamam
english: there for a thousand aeons he dwells, encircled by a hundred women, living upon the nectar-draught, supreme and like the elixir of immortality.

sanskrit: ṣaḍviṃśe divase yas tu prāśnīyād ekabhojanam sadā dvādaśa māsāṃs tu niyato niyatāśanaḥ
english: But he who eats a single meal on the twenty-sixth day, ever for twelve months, self-restrained and measured in his eating,

sanskrit: jitendriyo vītarāgo juhvāno jātavedasam sa prāpnoti mahābhāgaḥ pūjyamāno 'psarogaṇaiḥ
english: his senses subdued and his passions stilled, pouring oblations into Jātavedas, the fire — that illustrious man attains his reward, honored by hosts of apsarases.

sanskrit: saptānāṃ marutāṃ lokān vasūnāṃ cāpi so 'śnute vimāne sphāṭike divye sarvaratnair alaṃkṛte
english: He gains the worlds of the seven Maruts and of the Vasus, upon a heavenly chariot of crystal, adorned with every jewel.

sanskrit: gandharvair apsarobhiś ca pūjyamānaḥ pramodate dve yugānāṃ sahasre tu divye divyena tejasā
english: Honored by gandharvas and apsarases, he rejoices for two thousand divine ages, radiant with celestial splendor.

sanskrit: saptaviṃśe tu divase yaḥ prāśed ekabhojanam sadā dvādaśa māsāṃs tu juhvāno jātavedasam
english: He who eats a single meal on the twenty-seventh day, ever for twelve months pouring oblations into Jātavedas, the fire,

sanskrit: phalaṃ prāpnoti vipulaṃ devaloke ca pūjyate amṛtāśī vasaṃs tatra sa vitṛptaḥ pramodate
english: attains an abundant reward and is honored in the world of the gods; dwelling there and feeding on nectar, fully content, he rejoices.

sanskrit: devarṣicaritaṃ rājan rājarṣibhir adhiṣṭhitam adhyāvasati divyātmā vimānavaram āsthitaḥ
english: That realm trodden by the divine sages, O king, and ruled over by royal sages, the heavenly-souled one inhabits, seated upon his choice chariot.

sanskrit: strībhir manobhirāmābhī ramamāṇo madotkaṭaḥ yugakalpasahasrāṇi trīṇy āvasati vai sukham
english: Revelling with women that ravish the mind, flushed with delight, he dwells in bliss for three thousand age-aeons.

sanskrit: yo 'ṣṭāviṃśe tu divase prāśnīyād ekabhojanam sadā dvādaśa māsāṃs tu jitātmā vijitendriyaḥ
english: And he who eats a single meal on the twenty-eighth day, ever for twelve months, his self conquered and his senses wholly mastered,

sanskrit: phalaṃ devarṣicaritaṃ vipulaṃ samupāśnute bhogavāṃs tejasā bhāti sahasrāṃśur ivāmalaḥ
english: attains the abundant reward of the realm trodden by the divine sages; abounding in delights, he shines with splendor, spotless as the thousand-rayed sun.

sanskrit: sukumāryaś ca nāryas taṃ ramamāṇāḥ suvarcasaḥ pīnastanorujaghanā divyābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ
english: And tender, radiant women, full-breasted, with rounded thighs and hips, decked in heavenly ornaments, take their delight with him,

sanskrit: ramayanti manaḥ kāntā vimāne sūryasaṃnibhe sarvakāmagame divye kalpāyutaśataṃ samāḥ
english: those beloved ones delight his mind upon a chariot bright as the sun, heavenly and going wherever desire may lead, for a hundred myriad aeons of years.
